title: Scorecard SLI Mapping and Table Samples
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a working playbook for translating low-level SLIs (latency, uptime, cost/token, cache hit-rate) into QBR-facing KPIs and renewal signals. Goal: give CSMs a concrete checklist and sample tables to populate the QBR slide deck and renewal readiness tracker. This is intentionally operational and example-driven — use it as a fillable template during the 2–4 weeks before a renewal.

How to use this doc
- Step 1 (collect): Pull per-customer SLI exports for the quarter (daily aggregates + request-distribution histogram).
- Step 2 (normalize): Normalize token counts and cost units to the account's billing SKU.
- Step 3 (map): Apply the SLI-to-KPI mapping rules below.
- Step 4 (grade): Assign a green/amber/red grade to each KPI.
- Step 5 (action): Attach a single prioritized action per KPI.

Core SLI definitions (operational)
1) Latency (response generation time)
- Definition: Time from request accepted by our API gateway to final token emission for non-streaming responses. For streaming responses, measure time to first token + tokens/second tail.
- Metrics reported: p50, p90, p99 (ms); median first-token time (ms).
- Notes: For multimodal flows or tool-calling, isolate pure text-generation subcalls.
- Suggested SLOs: p90 < 350ms for small prompts (<256 tokens), p90 < 700ms for long prompts (>=256 tokens). Adjust per-customer SLA tier.

2) Uptime (availability)
- Definition: Fraction of successful API responses over total requests, excluding scheduled maintenance windows and excluding client error classes (4xx) for SLA calculation.
- Metrics reported: monthly uptime %, number of incidents contributing to downtime, mean time to recovery (MTTR).
- Suggested SLOs: 99.9% for hosted enterprise customers, 99.5% for standard tiers.

3) Cost per token (unit economics)
- Definition: Average compute and platform cost attributed to a single token produced (USD/token). Includes GPU runtime, memory and inference cache costs, and apportioned infra overheads. Not invoice price.
- Metrics reported: median cost/token, weighted-mean cost/token (weight by requests), 75th percentile cost/token to highlight heavy requests.
- Notes: For QBR, show delta vs. baseline quarter and identify primary drivers (long-context, high sampling, multi-pass evals).

4) Cache hit rate (inference prefix/KV cache effectiveness)
- Definition: Fraction of requests where the runtime served one or more tokens from a cache layer (prefix cache or KV cache) vs computed fresh.
- Metrics reported: overall cache-hit %, cache-hit % per route, cache-hit % on top-10 templates.
- Suggested SLOs: target > 40% for stable prompt-based workloads; flag anything < 20% for review.
- Notes: Cache hit rate interacts with cost/token and latency; high hit rate usually reduces both.

Translating SLIs into QBR KPIs (operator rules)
- KPI naming convention: <Outcome> — <Measure> — <Period> (e.g., "Prod latency — p90 (ms) — qtr"). Keep names short in slides.
- Group KPIs into: Performance, Reliability, Economics, and Behavioral Signals.
- Each KPI must have: definition (one sentence), measurement window, current value, target, trend (up/down/stable), status (green/amber/red), and owner action.

Scoring & signal thresholds (suggested)
- Performance (Latency): Green if p90 <= target; Amber if p90 <= 1.5x target; Red otherwise.
- Reliability (Uptime): Green >= SLO, Amber >= SLO - 0.2pp, Red < SLO - 0.2pp.
- Economics (Cost/token): Green if quarter-over-quarter delta <= +5% or trending down; Amber if +5–20%; Red if > +20% without mitigation plan.
- Cache (Hit rate): Green >= target, Amber if within 10 percentage points below target, Red if >10pp below target.

Special signal: Traffic mixture coefficient (TMC)
- Why: Two customers with identical p90 but different request distributions (many small vs few huge) can have different renewal risk. TMC is a lightweight indicator: fraction of tokens generated by top 5% of requests.
- Use: If TMC > 0.6 and cost/token is rising, prioritize cost-optimization playbook (quantization, prompt engineering, batching).

Sample KPI table (copy into QBR slide)
Columns: KPI | Definition | Current | Target | QoQ delta | Trend | Status | Action owner/action
Example rows: (use this exact table as a quick paste into slides)
KPI | Definition | Current | Target | QoQ delta | Trend | Status | Action owner/action
Prod latency — p90 (ms) | end-to-end gen p90, customer-prod | 420 ms | 350 ms | +18% | up | amber | Diego — investigate long-context kernel (Q2 plan)
Uptime — monthly % | availability excluding 4xx | 99.92% | 99.95% | -0.03pp | down | amber | Emma — run incident postmortem + backlog fix
Cost / token (USD) | compute + infra per token | $0.0068 | $0.0058 | +17% | up | amber | Ravi — propose caching profile change + batching
Cache hit rate — global % | prefix + KV cache hits | 26% | 45% | -4pp | down | red | Priya — propose template consolidation workshop
TMC (top5% token share) | fraction tokens from top 5% requests | 0.62 | 0.40 | +0.12 | up | red | Solutions — prioritize heavy-request review

Mini guidance on action types
- Performance actions: change model variant, reduce sampling, enable turbo-kernels, or tune batching window.
- Reliability actions: add dedicated capacity or change routing/fallback policy, increase retries with jitter.
- Economics actions: enable KV/prefix caching, reduce context window, use quantized variant, or add input-side truncation.
- Behavioral actions: run prompt standardization workshop, customer-side request throttling, or template consolidation.

Slide-ready copy (one-liners for exec)
- "Prod p90 up 18% QoQ driven by long-context inference; plan: enable 8-bit kernels and reduce default beam size for bulk endpoints."
- "Cost/token +17% QoQ: heavy evaluation workloads concentrated in 2 routes (TMC 0.62). Proposal: isolate evals to dedicated capacity and enable caching on stable templates."

Quickfill checklist for the QBR workbook (3 tabs)
1) Executive summary (1 page): 3 bullets — overall health, top risk, ask (e.g., capacity credit, optimization project).
2) KPI sheet (this doc's table): fill one row per KPI; color-code status.
3) Action tracker: owner, ETA, impact estimate (tokens saved/month, latency improvement ms).

Example action tracker row (copyable)
Owner | Action | ETA | Expected impact | Dependencies | Jira
Ravi Shah | Turn on prefix cache for route /v1/chat/generate | 2025-03-15 | -12% cost/token, +70ms p90 improvement | infra config + customer opt-in | CS-5123

Open questions / research hooks
- How granular should the cost/token allocation be for multi-tenant Dedicated pools? (proposal: allocate by token-weighted share per route).
- Do we want to add a "regression alert" KPI in QBR for model-quality drift? (early prototype: cross-quarter BLEU/embedding similarity delta).

Appendix: example queries to pull SLIs (engineering cheat-sheet)
- Latency p90 per route: SELECT percentile_disc(0.90) OVER() FROM request_latencies WHERE team_id = 'cust-XXX' AND quarter = '2025Q1';
- Cache hit rate: SUM(case when cache_used then 1 else 0 end)/COUNT(*) GROUP BY route;
- Cost/token: total_compute_cost / total_tokens_generated (join invoices+runtime logs).

Notes from last run (practical tips)
- Always show a small sample of heavy requests (top 3 by token count) to the customer — it converts faster to "we need controls" than abstract % numbers.
- Use the TMC to prioritize whether to recommend Dedicated capacity or a config-level optimization.
- Be explicit about unknowns: if cost/token includes burst credits or discounts, annotate the KPI row so finance can reconcile.

If you use this doc in a QBR, please paste the KPI table into the slide and attach the action tracker row(s) as a separate slide. Ping me (Priya) on Slack if you need a quick review before the customer meeting.
